title: New phone updates make video editing and screen styling easier than ever
summary:
Instagram and the phone maker Nothing are both launching new software updates to make video editing and phone customization much easier.

First, Instagram is rolling out a new tool called First Draft to help people create short videos, known as Reels. This feature automatically trims out quiet pauses and silent moments from your video clips. It does the boring work of cleaning up your videos so you can focus on the creative parts. To use it, you just select your clips, tap a button, and the app places them neatly on a timeline. This tool uses machine learning, which is a type of computer system that learns how to perform tasks on its own. It will arrive on Apple iPhones first before coming to other devices.

Meanwhile, the phone company Nothing is launching its new phone software, called Nothing OS 5.0. An operating system, or OS, is the main software that makes your phone run. This update is based on Android 17 and begins its open beta, which is a public test version, on August 26 for the Nothing Phone 3. The update lets you color-match your apps and widgets to your wallpaper. It also has a new app to control the glowing LED lights on the back of the phone, which are called Glyph lights. There are also new widgets, including an "Away Time" widget that tracks how long you spend away from your screen. Sadly, older devices like the Phone 1 will not get this update.

These updates matter to you because they take the chore out of everyday phone tasks. Instead of spending 10 minutes cutting silent gaps from a clip, or struggling to make your home screen look neat, your phone does the hard work. It gives you a much faster, cleaner, and more personal way to use your device every day.

You can expect to see these changes rolling out to compatible devices over the next few months.

title: A Popular Social Media Trick Ends as a Top Indie Game Goes on Sale
summary:
A popular way to read social media posts has been shut down, while a highly rated video game has just received a major price cut. 

The social media platform X, formerly known as Twitter, has forced a tool called Nitter to close by sending its creator a legal warning letter in August 2026. Nitter was a free, open-source project, which means its software code was built by volunteers and shared openly for anyone to use. The service was loved by many because it let people read public posts on X without logging in, downloading the app, or seeing ads. X accused the tool of scraping, which is a process where a computer program automatically pulls data off a website. 

This matters to you because major tech companies are increasingly blocking these helpful third-party tools. They want to force everyone to log into their official apps so they can track your online activity and show you targeted ads. If you want to keep up with public news on X, you will now likely have to create a real account and log in. 

Fortunately, if you need a new way to spend your screen time, there is a fantastic deal on a hit video game. A strange and highly praised game called Inscryption is currently on sale on the Humble store for only $7.99, down from its usual price of $20. This massive discount arrived right after the game's developer shared a new trailer for his next project at a major European gaming showcase.

Inscryption starts out as a spooky card game where you build a deck of moves to defeat an opponent. However, the game soon evolves into a mind-bending mystery that breaks all the rules of typical gaming. It is compatible with Windows, Mac, and Linux computers. If you want to escape the social media drama for a few hours, this budget-friendly game is a great place to start.

title: Smart Voice AI and Faster Supercomputers Are Upgrading Our Tech
summary:
Artificial intelligence is getting a major upgrade on two fronts: how companies talk to you, and how the supercomputers training these systems talk to each other. On the customer side, an AI voice company called Ringg just raised $10 million in new funding. This brings its total early-stage funding to $15.5 million. Ringg already processes 20 million call attempts a month. Instead of making simple robocalls, these AI agents handle complex tasks. For example, they can book doctor appointments or help you buy items you left in your online shopping cart. Ringg plans to partner with offshore support hubs to bring these smart assistants to companies in the US and beyond.

Why this matters to you: You will soon talk to much more capable AI assistants when you call customer support, and the systems powering them will run faster and cheaper.

To build these smart tools, tech companies must connect thousands of powerful computer chips. Meta recently introduced a new networking technology called MetaRoCE to help these chips share data much faster. Right now, training AI is like a group project where everyone has to wait for the slowest person. If one packet of data gets lost in the network, the whole system slows down. MetaRoCE fixes this by letting data arrive in any order. This means the computer chips never have to stop and wait.

Meta currently uses hundreds of thousands of computer chips to train its AI. Because these networks are so massive, even tiny delays can waste a lot of expensive computing power. Meta plans to release the official blueprints for this new networking system by October 2026. As both the physical networks and the friendly voices of AI improve, our daily interactions with technology will only get smoother.

title: Meta Faces Court Battles Over Teen Safety While US Government Raises Tech Visa Fees
summary:
Big tech companies are facing a double headache this week as Meta fights a major lawsuit over teen safety and the US government raises hiring fees. 

In a recent court trial, Instagram boss Adam Mosseri testified about how his app affects young people. He claimed he did not know his own staff had hid worrying safety data from him. Internal company reports from 2023 showed that teenagers were seeing high amounts of content about eating disorders and self-harm. In fact, teens saw this harmful content at much higher rates than adults. The court also heard that Instagram's "take a break" feature, which reminds kids to stop scrolling, was only used by 1.8 percent of users after it launched in 2021. A judge even questioned why design leaders did not know the basic safety numbers for their own app.

This matters to you because it shows how social media companies handle the mental health of young users. If you or your children use these apps, it reveals how difficult it is to get teens to log off, even with safety tools in place.

At the same time, the US government is making it much harder for tech giants to hire staff. The government is introducing a massive fee of over $103,265 for H-1B visas. This visa is a special permit that allows US companies to temporarily hire highly skilled workers from other countries. Tech giants like Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft use these visas the most. This huge cost will not just affect tech. It could also hurt rural hospitals and schools that rely on skilled foreign workers. Business leaders worry that these fees will force companies to set up offices and hire people outside of the US instead.

Between pressure over child safety and rising costs to hire top talent, tech giants are facing a very challenging time. We will have to wait and see how these big changes affect the gadgets and apps we use every day.

title: Big changes at OpenAI and a bright new Garmin smartwatch
summary:
This week, 2 major stories hit the technology world as artificial intelligence leader OpenAI lost another top boss, while Garmin revealed a powerful new smartwatch.

To start, OpenAI is dealing with a lot of empty seats in its offices. The head of their data centers, Chris Malone, recently left the company. Data centers are the massive, warehouse-sized buildings filled with computer servers that power AI tools like ChatGPT. Malone is just 1 of 13 high-profile executives to leave OpenAI in 2026. This list of departures includes the company's chief operating officer and chief marketing officer. OpenAI says these changes are part of normal growth, but the timing is tricky as the company prepares to sell shares to the public on the stock market for the first time.

On the gadget side, Garmin just unveiled its new Fenix 9 rugged smartwatch series, which launches on August 28. The basic model starts at $999.99 and features a beautiful OLED screen. OLED is a type of high-tech display that makes colors look incredibly vibrant. This screen is 2 times as bright as the older model, making it easy to read in direct sunlight. The watch also has more computer memory, which helps you swipe through digital maps much faster without any lag.

Why does all of this matter to you? The changes at OpenAI could affect how quickly your favorite AI tools get updated in the future. Meanwhile, if you love outdoor adventures, Garmin's new watch brings serious safety features. The Pro version starts at $1,099.99 and offers satellite connectivity so you can send messages even when you have no phone signal. It also offers a solar-charging screen that can push the battery life up to 57 days. These 2 updates show that the tech world is changing faster than ever.

title: The Next Wave of AI is Leaving the Cloud and Entering Your Home
summary:
A young robotics company called Generalist just reached a massive $3 billion valuation, showing how eager investors are to put smart brains into physical machines. Founded in 2024, the startup has now raised $600 million to build artificial intelligence models that act as general brains for different types of robots. Their newest system allows a robot to learn a brand-new physical chore just by watching a video clip that is only 3 to 12 seconds long. Tech investors hope this will lead to a breakthrough moment where robots can do various daily tasks without being reprogrammed every single time.

At the same time, other tech companies are working hard to make sure AI can run smoothly on the portable gadgets we use every day. A firm called Liquid AI recently released a free, open-source testing tool called Pipette. This tool helps software developers test how fast and reliably an AI model runs directly on everyday devices, like the latest smartphones and laptops, rather than relying on giant, distant computer warehouses.

Why does this matter to you? In the near future, we will want our home devices, smart cars, and personal robots to think for themselves instantly, even without an internet connection. Pipette measures the "quantization" of a model, which is a technical term for shrinking a massive AI program so it can fit onto a smaller microchip. This helps tech creators ensure that an AI helper on your phone or home device does not lag or drain your battery.

We are still in the early days of these technologies. However, as massive funding pours into smart robotics and better tools are built to test on-device systems, we are moving closer to a world where our physical gadgets are truly intelligent companions.

title: Driverless cars are heading to Europe and Apple just cut prices on a popular accessory
summary:
Big changes are coming to the tech world this week, from driverless cars expanding across Europe to a surprisingly cheap new accessory from Apple.

To start, the self-driving car company Waymo is planning to bring its robotic vehicles to Munich, Germany by 2027. Waymo makes autonomous cars, which are vehicles that can drive themselves without a human operator. The company will start testing its cars with backup safety drivers on Munich streets in the coming weeks. Waymo wants to get the official permits it needs to offer fully driverless rides to the public by next year. If you live in London, you might see them even sooner, as rides could start there as early as next month. Waymo is also setting up offices in other European countries, including France, Spain, Switzerland, and the Netherlands.

At the same time, Apple has quietly lowered the price of a popular accessory. The company is now selling its cleaning cloth for $9 instead of the original $19. This is the exact same soft cloth as before. It is made from a material that will not scratch your screens. It is safe to use on delicate displays, including nano-texture glass. This is a special matte screen designed to stop glare from light. While Apple recently released new computer models like the Mac Mini, those devices do not come with screens. But if you buy a separate monitor to go with them, this newly discounted cloth is a great way to keep it clean. The cloth still works on a huge list of older devices, going all the way back to the iPhone 5 from 2012.

These updates matter because they show how everyday technology is shifting. Self-driving travel is quickly becoming a reality for more people outside of the US. Meanwhile, even the most expensive tech companies are willing to offer a rare bargain on the small items we use every day.

Whether you are looking forward to a futuristic taxi ride or just want a cheaper way to keep your phone screen clean, tech is getting a bit more accessible.

title: Why Security Worries Are Affecting Your Video Games and Cars
summary:
Tech security is causing some major shakeups this week, affecting both the video games we play and the electric cars we want to buy. These 2 developments show that digital safety is no longer just about your laptop. Why does this matter? It proves that security issues can quietly disrupt your entertainment and your everyday transportation.

First, gamers need to be very careful online. The eagerly awaited game Grand Theft Auto 6 is not coming out until November 19, 2026. However, online hackers are already using the hype to trick excited players. They have built fake websites that offer a free, playable demo of the game. If you click to download it, you actually get hit with malware. This is harmful software that sneaks onto your device to steal your private passwords and web browser data. This scam is especially dangerous because the stolen data can let hackers log into your accounts, even if you have extra security codes set up.

At the same time, the electric vehicle world is facing its own digital security battle. The car brand Polestar will stop selling its vehicles in the US starting with its 2027 models. This is because of a US government ban on connected software from countries like China. Connected software is the computer technology inside a vehicle that links it to the internet. Because Polestar has a Chinese parent company, the US government blocked their sales due to security concerns. Polestar tried to offer solutions like regular data checks, but the government rejected them. Now, US car dealers are even suing the company over the sudden exit.

These 2 updates show us how important digital safety has become in our daily lives. Whether you are downloading a new game or shopping for a high-tech vehicle, technology is always connected. It is always a good idea to stay cautious and double-check where your software is coming from.

title: How New AI Tools Are Helping Us Map Out the Future
summary:
Scientists at MIT have built a new AI tool that can predict extreme weather events that have never happened before. Typically, weather models look at past disasters to guess what future storms will look like. This new tool uses math and daily weather maps to show worst-case scenarios, like a massive storm that is far worse than anything in the history books. For example, it can show a city how to prepare for 300 millimeters of rain, even if that city has only ever seen 200 millimeters. 

This matters to you because it helps local governments build better sea walls and emergency plans before a historic disaster strikes. At the same time, other companies are using AI to help us visualize our everyday ideas. A popular presentation startup called Gamma just bought a smaller design startup called Lica to create a new research lab. Gamma is currently worth $2.1 billion, and Lica raised $4 million in 2024 to help build these tools.

This new business partnership aims to change how we share information. Lica is known for turning simple screen recordings and screenshots into professional marketing videos and slideshows. By working together, the companies want to make presentations that are highly interactive. They want to build a system where the AI automatically adjusts the design and style of a slideshow depending on who is watching it. 

Both of these updates show that AI is moving away from just copying the past. Whether it is a city planner prepping for a 100-year storm or a business owner pitching a new idea, these tools are designed to help us see and plan for what comes next. It will be exciting to see how these tools make our lives safer and our work easier in the coming years.

title: Two New Handheld Gadgets Are Changing How We Play and Write on the Go
summary:
Two exciting new portable gadgets are coming to store shelves to change how we play games and work on the go. ASUS has revealed a premium handheld gaming computer, while TCL has built a gentle tablet designed to feel like a real paper notebook.

ASUS is celebrating the 20th anniversary of its gaming division with the ROG Ally X20. This portable gaming PC features a 7.4-inch OLED screen. OLED is a display technology that makes colors look incredibly vibrant and dark areas look truly black. This new model costs $1,300, which is a jump from the previous $1,000 model. It comes with a fast processor, which is the main computer brain, 24GB of memory, and a long-lasting battery. For a massive $2,499, you can even buy a bundle that includes smart glasses to project your games onto a giant virtual screen in front of your eyes. Pre-orders are open now, and sales begin on October 15.

On the other hand, if you want to relax and write, the new TCL Note A1 tablet offers a much calmer experience. It is a color tablet with a matte screen that does not reflect light. It comes with a stylus, which is a digital pen, that uses haptics. Haptics are tiny, smart vibrations that recreate the physical sensation of a real pencil scratching on paper. This device sits between a standard tablet and an E-Ink screen, which is the slow, power-saving screen technology used in electronic book readers. You can watch color videos on this tablet, but its main home screen is designed to keep you focused on writing.

This matters to you because portable devices are becoming highly specialized for our daily habits. Instead of buying a generic tablet, you can now choose a screen tailored precisely to how you want to spend your time. Whether you want to play high-end games on a gorgeous display or escape screen glare to write your thoughts down, these new options have you covered. Both devices are launching soon to help upgrade your mobile life.

title: Two exciting new tech gadgets are on the way for your wrist and your hands
summary:
There are 2 major new gadgets available for pre-order right now that aim to change how we monitor our health and play video games. 

This wearable is called the Luffu Link. It is a $250 health and safety wristband designed by the people who originally started Fitbit. It does not have a screen, and it comes in 3 colors. The band uses built-in LTE, which is cellular wireless technology that lets you send messages even if you do not have your phone with you. It tracks your sleep, heart rate, and steps. Users can also record quick voice notes to track their daily medication or meals. If you fall or need help, you can press a button to send your GPS location and a voice message to your family. It is designed to help people look after aging parents or family members without making them feel constantly watched. This helpful wristband will start shipping in early 2027.

Another device is a high-end portable gaming computer called the Xbox Ally X20. You can now pre-order this handheld console on its own for $1,300, and it will ship on October 15. The biggest update is its 7.4-inch OLED screen. OLED is a screen technology that offers much better contrast, making colors look extremely bright and dark areas look truly black. This model also features comfortable hand grips and a better control pad. While it is quite expensive, it is built for gamers who want the ultimate visual experience. Other older versions of this console will stay on sale for lower prices.

These new releases matter because they show how technology is becoming more specialized for our specific daily needs. Whether you want to keep your family safe with simple, screen-free tracking, or you want a top-tier visual experience for gaming on the go, there are exciting new tools on the horizon. We will have to wait and see how they perform in real life once they finally arrive.

title: AI is Learning to Do Our Daily Chores and Office Work
summary:
Artificial intelligence is moving beyond simple chatting to actually doing real work for us, both on our computers and in the physical world. Tech giant OpenAI is rolling out new tools to handle complex office tasks, while a robotics startup has built a brain that lets robots learn physical chores just by watching a short video. Together, these developments show how AI is becoming a practical helper in our daily lives.

On the digital side, OpenAI is pushing what they call "AI agents" through a new service called ChatGPT Work, included in their $20 monthly subscription. AI agents are smart software assistants that can perform entire, multi-step tasks on their own rather than just answering questions or writing text. The company wants to make this powerful tech incredibly easy to use. Instead of typing complicated commands, you can simply speak to the system naturally, like talking to a friend, and let the AI do the heavy lifting behind the scenes.

Meanwhile, robots are getting a similar upgrade in the physical world. A company called Generalist AI recently shared details about its new robot brain, called GEN-1.5. This is a "foundation model," which is a large AI program trained on massive amounts of data. Using a trick called "physical prompting," you can show the robot a video demonstration of a physical task lasting only 3 to 12 seconds. The robot can then copy the action immediately without any extra programming. It can successfully copy physical tasks 59% of the time on its first try, and that number jumps to 83% after just 5 minutes of practice. It can even watch a human hand do something and copy it with its own robotic hand.

Why does this matter to you? It means we are getting closer to a world where you do not need to know how to code to use advanced technology. Whether you want a digital assistant to organize your business files or a physical robot to help sweep the floor, you will soon be able to just show or tell them what you need. AI is quickly transforming from a fun novelty into a genuinely useful tool for everyone.

title: How We Spend Online: From $600 Gaming Speakers to Crowdfunding Lifelines
summary:
ASUS has launched its first-ever gaming soundbar for $600, while fundraising site GoFundMe has grown into a major digital safety net. These two developments show the very different ways we use technology today. Some of us are buying high-end gear for entertainment. Others are using digital platforms just to get by. Both show how much we rely on the internet in our daily lives.

The new ASUS speaker is called the ROG Gjallar. It costs $600 and is built for people who play online games with friends. It comes with a special control hub and built-in microphones. These microphones block out background noise so you can talk to teammates clearly without wearing a headset. The soundbar also uses Dolby Atmos. This is a special audio technology that makes three-dimensional sound bounce around your room. It also includes a wireless subwoofer, which is a separate speaker that produces deep bass sounds.

Meanwhile, other tech tools are helping people survive hard times. Tim Cadogan, the chief executive of GoFundMe, recently discussed how his website became a crucial backup plan starting in 2020. GoFundMe is a for-profit company that operates in 20 countries. Even though it is a business, it has become a primary way for people to pay for medical bills, fund local projects, or get help after disasters. It acts as a safety net when people have nowhere else to turn.

Why does this matter to you? It shows that technology is about much more than just fancy gadgets. The internet is now where we go to find joy, build communities, and seek help during emergencies. Whether you want to upgrade your gaming setup or support someone in need, technology connects us all. It is a powerful reminder of how digital tools shape our modern world.

title: A Cure for Car Sickness and a Big Move in Space Stock
summary:
2 major tech updates are making headlines this week, ranging from big financial moves in space to a new feature on your smartphone. First, financial records show that Donald Trump bought up to $50,000 worth of SpaceX stock back in June. This happened just 2 weeks after the rocket company held its IPO, which is when a private company first offers its shares to the public. The stock was trading around $150 at the time, but it has since dropped back to its starting price of $135. This means the investment might currently be losing money. Representatives say a financial firm manages the portfolio to match big indexes, which are collections of top stocks. Because SpaceX lobbied to join these index groups quickly, many everyday investors might actually own a piece of the company without knowing it.

Meanwhile, Google is releasing a helpful new tool for your phone that aims to stop car sickness. The feature is called Motion Assist, and it is coming to Android 17. If you ever feel dizzy or nauseous when looking at your phone in a moving car, this tool is built for you. Motion sickness usually happens because your eyes are looking at a still screen, but your inner ear can feel the car turning and stopping. 

To fix this, Motion Assist uses your phone’s built-in motion sensors to put tiny dots around the edge of your screen. These dots glide across your screen in the same direction the car is moving. If the car turns left, the dots move right, which helps your brain realize you are in motion. You can change the shape and color of these dots, and the feature can even turn on by itself when it senses you are driving.

This matters because tech is not just about giant rocket companies changing the stock market. It is also about small, smart updates that make our daily lives much more comfortable. If you use an Android phone, you can check your settings soon to see if the new update has arrived.

title: How Driverless Cars and Sharp TV Screens Are Changing Our World
summary:
Technology is moving fast today, bringing both self-driving cars to our streets and smarter tools to make our old videos look crystal clear. 

This matters to you because these changes will shape what you see on your home television and how safe you feel when walking down the road. 

To start, let us look at self-driving cars, which are also called robotaxis. Companies like Waymo now have 3,500 of these driverless cars running in 11 cities in the US. Some companies, like Zoox, are even starting paid rides in Las Vegas. However, many people are pushing back against them. In San Francisco, these cars have blocked traffic and got in the way of police and fire trucks. Because of this, states like New York have stopped plans to allow them, and cities are asking for tighter rules.

At the same time, tech companies are working on making old movies and home videos look better on modern screens. They do this by converting old videos into 4K, which is a very sharp screen resolution. To do this, computer software must upscale the video, which means blowing up the image to fit a larger screen. The software has to add a massive number of new pixels, which are the tiny dots of color that make up a picture. Because the software has to guess what the new dots should look like, the final video can sometimes look blurry or unnatural. To get a perfect picture, professionals still have to go back to original physical film reels, which can take 3 years and cost over $12 million.

Both of these new technologies show that while the future is exciting, it still has some bugs to work out. We will have to wait and see how these tools improve over the next few years.

title: Big tech updates: Oura prepares for a massive launch while Lenovo faces a gaming glitch
summary:
This week, we have big news from the tech world, featuring a massive financial move from a popular smart ring maker and some stressful software issues for handheld gamers. First, Oura is reportedly planning a US IPO as early as September. An IPO, or initial public offering, is when a private company sells its stock to the public on the stock market for the first time. Reports say this move could value Oura at more than $16 billion. That is a huge jump from its $10.9 billion value last year. The company is growing fast, with revenue expected to climb from $500 million in 2024 to nearly $2 billion by 2026. However, it is not all good news. A new lawsuit accuses Oura of misleading customers about how accurately its ring tracks sleep, though Oura strongly denies these claims.

Meanwhile, gamers using the Lenovo Legion Go handheld console are dealing with a stressful update problem. Lenovo recently released a BIOS update, which is the core software that tells a computer's physical hardware how to start up. Sadly, this update has "bricked" some devices. This means the software caused a glitch that left the consoles completely dead and useless, like a heavy brick. Lenovo has now removed the update from its website. They suggest holding down the power button for 10 seconds if your screen goes black. Still, many gamers are upset about the prospect of paying high repair bills for a mistake made by the company.

These stories show why keeping an eye on tech companies matters to you. Whether we are wearing smart devices to track our health or playing games on a handheld screen, we rely heavily on these brands to keep things running smoothly. When things go wrong, we expect companies to stand by their products and help their customers. We will have to wait and see how both of these situations play out in the coming weeks.

title: AI is facing a reality check on Wall Street, but the actual tech is getting better
summary:
The artificial intelligence world is seeing a major split right now, with big-money investments facing government trouble while regular tech tools get smarter and cheaper. 

First, look at the financial side of AI. A famous AI-focused investment company called Situational Awareness is currently under investigation by US regulators. The Securities and Exchange Commission, or SEC, is asking banks for records about the fund. This comes after a massive drop in AI stock values in July 2024 erased billions of dollars. The fund was started by a former OpenAI employee and grew incredibly fast before the crash. Now, it is serving as a warning that the giant wave of AI money might be slowing down.

But while the big money is hitting a bump, the actual technology is still moving forward. A company called Fastino just released a new free AI tool called GLiNER2.5. This tool helps computers pull specific details out of huge documents, like finding names in contracts or medical records. Normally, this task is either very expensive or requires giant computer chips. The new tool can read documents up to 4,096 words long. It uses a clever shortcut that measures where words start and end instead of scanning every single option. This means even a two-person company can use it on basic office computers without spending a fortune.

Why does this matter to you? It shows that the future of AI is not just about giant, expensive systems that cost millions of dollars to run. Instead, smaller and more efficient tools are making it easier for regular businesses to protect your private data, read contracts, and handle customer support. While Wall Street is worrying about a potential AI bubble bursting, software developers are quietly making tools that are actually useful for everyday life.

It turns out that the real value of AI might not be in the stock market, but in these quiet, practical upgrades.

title: Helpful New App Tools and Big Changes to Online Home Searching
summary:
Two big tech companies are making major changes this week to how you scroll through social media and search for rentals online. First, the popular social media app Threads is testing a handy new feature that automatically turns podcast audio into text. This process is called transcription, which simply means the app writes down the spoken words so you can read them on your screen. This tool will let you enjoy audio clips on your feed even when you have your phone on silent.

Why does this matter to you? If you are on a busy train or in a quiet office, you can still follow along with your favorite shows without needing your headphones. Meta, the company that owns Threads, wants to attract more audio creators to its platform. Since the app already reached a massive 500 million monthly users in June, adding these helpful tools makes the app much more useful for everyday people.

Meanwhile, there is big news if you are looking for a new place to live. The Federal Trade Commission, which is the US government agency that protects consumers, has settled a major legal case with the popular property websites Zillow and Redfin. The government accused the two companies of violating antitrust laws. These are rules that stop giant companies from making deals that block competition and lead to higher prices.

The government argued that a 2025 partnership between the two websites cut down on rental options, which made prices go up. To settle the case, Redfin must now restart its own rental advertising business to compete fairly with Zillow. This is a big win for renters and landlords because more website competition usually means more rental choices and better rental prices when you search for a home online.

Whether you are reading a podcast on your commute or searching for a new flat, these updates show how much tech companies shape our daily lives.

title: Safety Blocks and Startup Spots: The Newest Battles and Big Events in Tech
summary:
A big battle is heating up over 3D-printed guns, just as tech startups prepare for a massive industry event. 

In New York, a controversial developer has created a tool to bypass new safety laws on 3D printers. These printers are smart machines that can build physical objects out of plastic or metal using digital files. A recent state law requires new printers to run software that blocks gun designs. This software works by identifying a "hash," which is a unique digital fingerprint attached to each file. However, a new tool called "Hochulization" scrambles these digital fingerprints, allowing the files to bypass the block and print working weapons. 

This development comes as police report a rise in homemade, untraceable firearms. In New York, police seized just 1 of these weapons in 2021, but that number jumped to 109 in 2024. Many safety groups worry about this rise in weapons. Meanwhile, tech groups and makers argue that scanning files on private printers is an invasive form of digital spying. 

While some creators fight the law, others are looking to show off their inventions legally. The TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 conference will take place in San Francisco from October 13 to October 15 in 2026. Over 10,000 founders, investors, and tech leaders will gather at the event. Startups can book exhibit tables starting at $12,500 to pitch their products and find partners. These spaces are limited, and the deadline to book a spot is September 25, 2026. 

Why does this matter to you? The debate over 3D-printed guns shows how difficult it is for governments to regulate digital files. At the same time, massive tech shows like the one in 2026 are where the useful everyday gadgets of tomorrow are born. Technology is moving incredibly fast, bringing both serious challenges and exciting new ideas into our lives.

title: AI is Growing Up Fast with Smart Software and Walking Robots
summary:
The artificial intelligence boom is moving faster than ever, with massive amounts of cash flowing into both software and physical machines. Investors are betting billions of dollars that AI will soon run our offices and walk our streets. This trend is clear as 2 major tech firms show off massive growth and eye-watering valuations in 2026.

A company called Replit is changing how we create software. Replit makes a tool that helps everyday people write computer code using AI, even if they have never coded before. This simple idea has made the company incredibly valuable. Its worth jumped to $9 billion, and its annual sales are on track to reach $1 billion, up from just $2.8 million in 2024. The company's leader, Amjad Masad, is preparing to share his vision of a world where anyone can turn ideas into digital products instantly.

At the same time, AI is getting a physical body. A robotics company backed by carmaker XPENG just raised over $900 million to build a humanoid robot called IRON. Humanoid robots are machines built to look and move like humans. This robot has 76 joints for smooth movement and uses advanced chips to make quick decisions locally on the machine. The company hopes to mass-produce these robots by the end of 2026 and start deliveries in 2027.

These updates matter to you because they show how quickly AI is moving from our computer screens into our daily lives. Soon, you might use AI to build your own custom phone app, or you might see a humanoid robot working in a local store. We are moving toward a future where smart machines are no longer science fiction, but regular tools we use every day.

title: Big Tech Changes Are Coming to Your Apartment Search and Your TV Screen
summary:
Online real estate giant Zillow has settled a major government lawsuit, while sports giant ESPN is raising its streaming prices. 

The US Federal Trade Commission, which is a government group that protects shoppers, sued Zillow in 2025. Several states, including New York and Washington, also joined the legal fight. Government officials accused Zillow of paying its rival Redfin $100 million to stop listing rental apartments for up to 9 years. Under the new agreement, Redfin must launch its apartment search tool again with many more properties. This extra competition should help lower search costs for people looking to rent a home. Zillow must also let its business clients change their contracts for free and share employee info so Redfin can hire new staff. 

At the same time, sports fans will soon have to pay more to watch live games. Starting on September 17, ESPN is raising its streaming rates. The basic option with ads will rise from $12.99 to $13.99 a month. If you prefer to pay for a whole year, that basic plan will go from $129.99 to $139.99. The larger Unlimited plan will rise to $319.99 a year. Many popular TV bundles that package the sports app with Disney Plus and Hulu will also go up in price by $2 or $3 each month. This is the first price hike since the standalone sports channel launched last August with features like multi-screen viewing, which lets you watch more than 1 game at the same time on your TV. 

Why does this matter to you? If you are looking for a new flat or apartment, you will soon have more online choices to help you find a deal. But if you want to stream live sports, you may need to adjust your monthly budget. Keeping a close eye on your digital subscriptions can help you save cash on both housing and home entertainment.

title: How Video Games Are Teaching Tomorrow's Robots to Move
summary:
An exciting new artificial intelligence startup is using video game footage to teach robots how to move in the real world. The company is called General Intuition. It is growing incredibly fast. Big-name investors are currently in talks to fund the startup at a $6 billion valuation. This massive deal comes only a few weeks after the company raised $320 million at a $2.3 billion valuation.

General Intuition was started by the creator of a video game clip-sharing platform. It trains its AI using hundreds of millions of hours of gameplay. Specifically, it uses "action labels." These are simple records of exactly which buttons a player pressed on a controller and when they pressed them. Experts believe this teaches the AI how to make smart, human-like decisions. The startup wants to build "physical AI." This is smart software that helps actual robots navigate the physical world safely. The company will use its new money to hire more staff and buy more computer power to train its models.

Why does this matter to you? It means the games you play on your couch could soon help create smarter, safer robots for your home or workplace. Virtual environments are becoming the ultimate school for real-world machines.

Speaking of virtual worlds, game developers are already busy building the next generation of hits. The studio CD Projekt Red just announced that they want to launch their highly anticipated game, *The Witcher 4*, in 2028. This is a massive fantasy role-playing game where players explore a giant virtual world. While 2028 is a long wait, the studio has other plans. They will release a new expansion for *The Witcher 3* in 2027. They are also working on a multiplayer spin-off game too.

From smarter robots to bigger virtual worlds, the future of technology and gaming is looking incredibly bright.

title: Earbuds for Humans and Sprinting Robots Break New Running Records
summary:
We have some exciting news from the running world, featuring brand-new lightweight earbuds for humans and incredibly fast robots that do not know how to stop.

First, let us look at the track, where human athletic records are falling to machines. At the World Humanoid Robot Games, a special competition for robots built with 2 legs, a machine called Tiangong Ultra ran 100 meters in just 9.39 seconds. That is faster than Usain Bolt's famous world record of 9.58 seconds. Another robot called Lightning was close behind at 9.47 seconds. While these machines are incredibly fast, they still have 1 major problem. They do not know how to slow down, so they have to crash into soft pads at the finish line and get carried away on stretchers.

If you prefer to do your own running, you might want some new gear to help you along. Shokz has just released 2 new pairs of lightweight headphones for $130 each. The first is called the OpenFit Air 2. These earbuds weigh only 7.2g, which is about the same as a few paperclips. They use an open-ear design. This means they do not seal your ear canal, allowing you to hear traffic and stay safe in busy cities. They also feature special software to give you deeper bass and a richer sound.

The second model is called the OpenRun Air 2. These wrap around your head and use bone conduction. This is a smart technology that sends music vibrations through your cheekbones instead of directly into your ears. Both pairs of earbuds have great battery life. The OpenFit Air 2 lasts for 8 hours on a single charge, while the OpenRun Air 2 lasts for 10 hours.

This matters to you because technology is changing how we move, exercise, and stay safe. Whether you want a better way to listen to music on your daily jog or want to marvel at the future of robotics, technology is sprinting forward. Just remember to watch where you are going so you do not crash like the robots.

title: New Updates Bring Super-Private Phones and Cheaper Laptops Closer to You
summary:
Two big changes are coming to the gadgets we use every day, bringing better phone privacy and more affordable laptops.

First, a highly secure phone operating system called GrapheneOS is coming to Motorola devices in 2027. An operating system is the main software that runs a phone. GrapheneOS is a private version of the Android system that blocks tracking and protects your personal data. Right now, this software only works on Google Pixel phones. However, Google phones are becoming harder for developers to support. Soon, GrapheneOS will expand to high-end Motorola models, including their folding flip phones. Motorola is working directly with the software creators to build ultra-secure hardware. Cheaper Motorola phones might get this software later, but only if the company promises to support them with updates for 7 years.

Second, computer makers are finding new ways to build cheaper laptops that still run fast. A computer company called Chuwi just released the Unibook laptop for a starting price of $449. It uses a new budget processor, which is the main computer chip that acts as the brain of the laptop. This chip is made by Intel using modern technology, rather than using slow, outdated parts. Other brands like Dell and Acer are also releasing similar budget laptops starting between $599 and $699. While the Chuwi Unibook has a great keyboard and 8GB of memory, the trackpad is hard to use and the frame feels thin.

These updates matter because they give you more control over your data and your wallet. You will soon have more choices if you want a highly secure phone that does not track your moves. At the same time, computer brands are finally trying to build budget laptops that do not lag. Finding a great, cheap computer is still difficult because memory parts are expensive right now, but the options are slowly improving.

title: New Specialized AI Models Are Learning to Hunt Software Bugs and Read Legal Contracts
summary:
AI is getting much better at doing highly specialized professional jobs, from finding computer security bugs to reading complex legal agreements. Two new projects show how tech companies are training AI to tackle these difficult, multi-step tasks instead of just acting as basic chatbots.

First, a Beijing-based AI lab called Zhipu released a new coding model named GLM-5.3 on August 14. This model made waves by scoring 84.5% on a security test, which was slightly higher than top US models from OpenAI and Anthropic. This means the model is excellent at spotting software vulnerabilities, which are hidden flaws in computer code that hackers could exploit. However, the company admits its model still struggles with more complex tasks, like actually explaining how to fix or use those flaws. Because Zhipu plans to make this model open-weight—which means anyone can freely download and run the software code—it could make powerful security tools available to everyone.

Meanwhile, on August 20, 2026, a legal tech company named Harvey introduced a research project called Harvey Tenet. This is an AI designed specifically to do heavy-duty work for law firms, like reading through 10,000 documents to write legal memos or checking contracts for errors. Harvey built this by taking an existing open-weight model and training it with reinforcement learning, a method where the AI learns by trial and error to get virtual rewards for correct answers.

This matters to you because AI is moving out of the laboratory and into the tools we rely on every day. In the near future, these specialized programs could help secure the apps on your phone from cyberattacks, or help your lawyer review your house-buying paperwork much faster and cheaper.

We are quickly moving past the era of simple AI chatbots and entering a time when highly trained digital assistants do the heavy lifting for us.

title: Fast tech: Robots beat human runners while sports cars reach new speeds
summary:
High-tech machines are hitting incredible new speed records on both 2 legs and 4 wheels. At a recent robot sports event in Beijing, a humanoid robot ran the 100-meter dash in just 9.39 seconds. A humanoid robot is a machine built to look and move like a person. This amazing run actually beat the human world record of 9.58 seconds set by Usain Bolt in 2009. The winning robot was called the Tiangong Ultra, and it barely beat another fast model called the Lightning. However, these robots are not ready for normal jobs yet. They ran so fast that they crashed straight into safety pads at the finish line, and some even had to be carried off on stretchers. 

If you prefer your speed on wheels, modern sports cars are also pushing new limits. The famous Ford Mustang starts at $34,990 and can sprint from 0 to 60 miles per hour in 3.7 seconds. This "0 to 60" measurement tells us how quickly a car can go from a complete stop to highway speed. But other sports cars are getting even higher ratings from experts. The Maserati GranTurismo starts at $150,395 and can hit 60 miles per hour in a blistering 3.2 seconds. Another top choice is the BMW M4, which offers supreme speed and handles corners beautifully. 

Why does this matter to you? It shows how fast technology is developing in completely different areas. From the computer brains guiding robotic runners to the advanced engines inside sports cars, machines are becoming smarter and quicker than ever. You might not see a sprinting robot on your street or park a luxury supercar in your driveway anytime soon. Still, these fast designs give us an exciting preview of how future machines will move us.

title: How Giant Computers and Smart Digital Workers Are Changing Business
summary:
Artificial intelligence is growing rapidly in 2026, driven by massive computer warehouses and new smart software that can do office work on its own. 

To understand how this works, we have to look behind the scenes at the physical power of AI. Lately, specialized computer companies known as "neoclouds" have been booming. These are businesses that rent out giant arrays of computer chips called graphics processing units, or GPUs. You can think of GPUs as the heavy-duty brains that make AI think. Huge tech players like CoreWeave and Nebius are spending billions of dollars to build these systems. They are locking down gigawatts of electrical power—which is enough electricity to power whole cities—just to keep their servers running. In fact, CoreWeave made $2.58 billion in revenue in just 3 months during 2026.

All of this raw computer power is now trickling down into very practical business tools. For example, a shipping software company called Alvys recently launched a new platform called Foundry. This system uses "AI agents," which are smart programs designed to perform specific business tasks automatically, much like a human worker would. Instead of a person manually checking shipping paperwork, tracking trucks, or filing claims, these digital agents can do it all. The system even has built-in safety limits, so a human still has to sign off on big decisions or large payments.

Why does this matter to you? Even if you do not run a shipping business or buy giant computer chips, these developments will quietly change your daily life. As companies use these smart tools to cut down on office paperwork and track deliveries, businesses become much more efficient. In the long run, this makes shipping faster and helps keep the prices of everyday goods lower for everyone. 

AI is no longer just a fun tool for writing poetry or creating silly pictures. It is quickly becoming the unseen engine of our modern economy.

title: Smart Cars and Super Bright Lights: Upgrades for Your Daily Routine
summary:
From the screens in our cars to the lights in our pockets, everyday gadgets are getting some incredibly powerful upgrades. 

First, let us look at the confusing world of car screens. Many people do not know the difference between Android Auto and Android Automotive. Android Auto is a system that projects your phone screen onto your car dashboard. It acts like a second screen for your phone. On the other side, Android Automotive is an operating system, which is the main software built directly into the car. This means the car does its own thinking without needing a phone. It can even control your car's air conditioning and battery settings. Polestar became the first brand to use this built-in system in 2020. 

Next, let us look at everyday carry tools, often called EDC gear. These are useful items you carry with you every day. Pocket flashlights are now reaching unbelievable levels of brightness. Brightness is measured in lumens. While a normal flashlight uses a few hundred lumens, new models can pump out up to 10,000 lumens. For example, the Olight Marauder Mini costs about $200 and blasts 7,000 lumens of light. The Nitecore EDC37 costs around $140 and packs 8,000 lumens into a tiny body. If you want even more power, the Fenix LR35R shines at a massive 10,000 lumens. These devices recharge easily using a normal USB-C cable.

Why does this matter to you? Knowing these tech differences helps you buy the right gear. Built-in car software keeps your eyes on the road because you do not have to plug in your phone. Meanwhile, having a tiny flashlight that can light up an entire field makes power outages or dark walks much safer. Whether you are driving at night or walking the dog, these smart upgrades make daily life just a bit easier.

title: Why we need to brace for the new wave of AI hackers
summary:
The president of OpenAI is warning businesses that they must upgrade their digital security much faster to protect against smart, automated AI hackers. Recently, a group of automated AI systems working together managed to break into OpenAI's research network and another major AI platform called Hugging Face. The attackers did this by combining leaked internet passwords with hidden bugs in the software. This shows how quickly hacker tools are evolving, making it easier for them to find and exploit security gaps that humans might miss.

This matters to you because almost all of our daily services rely on secure software. Today, programmers use complex computer code to build everything from scientific data-processing tools to website servers. While this code can handle incredibly advanced tasks—like sorting through huge piles of scientific data or running mathematical calculations—it also contains hidden human mistakes. As AI gets smarter, it can scan millions of lines of this complex code in seconds. This is a double-edged sword: bad actors can use AI to find these security flaws, but defenders can use the exact same technology to patch them first.

To show how fast these new defense tools work, OpenAI’s co-founder Greg Brockman tested his own personal website. He used an advanced version of ChatGPT to scan his site for safety flaws. In just 15 minutes, the AI found 13 security issues, such as outdated software and unsafe connection settings. The AI then took about 1 hour to completely fix all of those problems.

In the end, keeping our digital world safe is becoming a fast-paced race. While AI-powered hackers are getting smarter, the tools to defend our data are growing just as quickly. Staying ahead will simply require companies to adopt these smart defense tools before the bad guys do.

title: How Hidden Tech Details Can Save You Money on TVs and Cars
summary:
This week, we are looking at how hidden technical details can affect your wallet, whether you are mounting a television or buying a luxury car. Knowing how to read these specifications matters because it keeps your home safe and protects you from bad investments. Taking a few minutes to study the facts before you buy will save you from major headaches later.

First, if you want to mount a TV, you must understand VESA. This stands for Video Electronics Standards Association. It is not a screen resolution, but simply the standard spacing between the screw holes on the back of your TV, measured in millimeters. For example, a 400 by 200 pattern means the holes are 400 millimeters apart sideways and 200 millimeters apart up and down. You can find your TV's pattern in the manual or by measuring the holes yourself. Many wall brackets support multiple sizes, so you just need to make sure your TV's pattern is on the list. However, a matching pattern is not enough. You must also check that the bracket can handle your TV's weight, and use the correct screws to keep it secure.

Meanwhile, tech and market shifts are hitting luxury car buyers. Maserati vehicles are famous for style, but they lose an average of 71% of their value after 5 years. Individual models like the Ghibli and Levante have dropped in value by around 69% to 72% in just 3 years. Buyers worry about poor reliability and high repair bills once the warranty ends. To make matters worse, dealers cut prices to move cars off the lot, which instantly hurts resale values. Maserati also pushed to make electric vehicles, or EVs, which run on battery power. But luxury buyers do not want electric versions, preferring traditional gas engines. This helped cause Maserati sales to drop from about 49,000 in 2017 to only 11,127 in 2025.

In both cases, taking a few minutes to do some research pays off. Checking weight limits and resale trends will keep your living room safe and your bank account happy.
